Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Nexus Energy Inc. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Nexus Energy Inc.'s Q2 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Michael Chen, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Jenkins, Chief Financial Officer; David Patel, Chief Operating Officer; and Sarah Thompson, VP of Exploration.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to Michael Chen.

Michael Chen: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Nexus Energy delivered solid results in Q2 2024, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices. We achieved impressive proved reserves additions, posting a reserve replacement ratio of 158% through robust organic growth. I'm particularly pleased with our progress on exploration and drilling activities, where key wells have exceeded expectations. We remain focused on maintaining disciplined debt levels and improving leverage ratios. Further, we are advancing our capital expenditure guidance with a clear emphasis on high-return projects. Finally, we are taking decisive steps to drive down lifting costs per BOE through innovative cost reduction initiatives.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you, Michael. As Michael noted, we had a strong quarter. Our revenue reached $2.75 billion, up 18% year-over-year, reflecting higher production volumes and realized prices averaging $78 per BOE amid WTI around $82 and Henry Hub gas at $2.80 per MMBtu supported by LNG demand. Operating income came in at $950 million, while net income was $650 million. We generated $850 million in free cash flow and returned $400 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases, including our progressive dividend now yielding 3.2%. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $5.2 billion in total debt and $800 million in cash and equivalents.

Let me expand on our balance sheet, which continues to anchor our financial strength amid commodity volatility. Specifically, our debt profile—including total debt, net debt, and leverage ratios—demonstrates meaningful progress compared to peers like Occidental, Pioneer, and EOG. At quarter-end June 30, 2024, total debt totaled $5.2 billion, made up of $4.1 billion in long-term senior notes, $800 million drawn on our $2.5 billion revolver, and $300 million in term loans linked mainly to Gulf of Mexico operations. This marks a slight 3% sequential uptick from Q1, tied to working capital needs and pre-funding some capex, but our blended cost of debt holds at a competitive 4.8%, with 85% fixed through maturities out to 2033. We refinanced $500 million of near-term notes into longer-dated paper at 4.25%, capturing 125 basis points of savings as rates stabilized.

Net debt, a key gauge for our cash-flowing E&P model, stood at $4.4 billion, down 12% year-over-year and 18% from 2022 peaks, powered by $1.2 billion in nine-month free cash flow—including $450 million in Q2 at solid realizations. We deployed $650 million to trim revolver and term debt, lifting cash to $800 million and leaving $1.7 billion undrawn capacity under $4.8 billion commitments. Leverage metrics advanced sharply: net debt to last-twelve-months EBITDAX improved to 1.4x from 2.1x a year ago, with LTM EBITDAX at $3.15 billion, up 22% on Permian strength and Eagle Ford redevelopment. This slots us favorably versus EOG at 0.8x, Pioneer around 1.0x, and Conoco at 1.2x, aiding potential rating upgrades. Debt-to-cap stands at 28%, down from 35%, bolstered by equity gains from strong reserves and a 20% dividend increase. Interest coverage is a healthy 12x, resilient even at $70 Brent with OPEC+ support.

By region, Permian assets (65% output) fuel deleveraging with $42 breakeven inventory and pad efficiencies yielding 25% FCF margins, covering 70% of paydowns via electric fracs and in-house sand. GoM (20% production) has higher debt from $900 million JV financing for tie-backs, offset by $110/bbl prices and 90% hedges despite weather events. International stakes, like Suriname, stay equity-funded until development.

Forward, deleveraging tops priorities amid service inflation and rates. A $1.5 billion monetization slate includes an $850 million Eagle Ford gas sale, proceeds to revolver. Hedges shield 65% 2024 oil at $75 and 55% gas at $3.50. Digital twins with Halliburton lift EURs 10%, bolstering covenants. We eye sub-1.2x leverage by year-end on $1.8 billion FCF, with 50% to debt, 30% returns, balance for M&A—primed for consolidation.

Shifting to operational efficiency, our lifting costs per BOE—a core measure of field-level LOE excluding non-cash items—have declined sharply, fueling FCF. Company-wide, Q2 hit $9.10 per BOE, down 14% YoY and 5% sequentially, our best ever, versus EOG's $9.80 and Pioneer's $9.50. Five-year trend: $14.50 in 2019, reset to $12.20 by 2021, peaked $13.80 in 2022, averaged $10.50 in 2023.

Regionally, Permian (65% output) led at $7.80, below basin $9-10 EIA average, via Midland factory mode. Eagle Ford (20%) improved to $10.50 from $14 amid 75% water cut, recycling 85% produced water. GoM at $18.20 for deepwater, down 22% YoY with ROV and electrification. Angola at $12.40, buoyed by 98% FPSO uptime.

Drivers: ops discipline via "Cost Zero"—deferred workovers 30%, ESP lives to 850 days ($0.80/BOE save); Eagle Ford chemical tweaks cut SWD 25%. Digital oilfield ($150 million invested) with SLB Delfi and Halliburton: AI flagged 15,000 failures, cut downtime 40% ($0.60/BOE); digital twins optimized child wells 12% EUR; GoM AUVs trimmed interventions 35%. Procurement: 70% tubulars/chemicals locked at 2022 prices with NOV/Baker Hughes; vendor consolidation 18% savings; "OneNexus" cross-training cut headcount 12%, LTIR 0.12.

This 25% CAGR drop since 2021 accretes $55 million FCF per $1/BOE. Peers like Conoco at $8.50 validate. Guide $9.30-$9.70 2024, sub-$8.50 2025, $7.00 by 2027 on 5% capex.

On reserves, Q2 marked a pivotal quarter in our long-term sustainability. Full-year trajectory points to 1.2 billion BOE PDP/PDNP additions, yielding 158% RRR versus 760 million BOE produced (5% up YoY). Organic share: 82% or 984 million BOE (129% organic RRR), up from 112% in 2022, beating 110% decade average, top-quartile vs. Exxon/EOG.

Per SEC: positive revisions 285 million BOE from frac/lateral gains—Permian laterals to 12,500 feet with ApexFlow proppant, 15-20% EUR uplift. Extensions/discoveries 512 million BOE (14 extensions, 3 wildcats); Eagle Ford 3D seismic added 180 million at $8.50 F&D. Improved recovery 187 million BOE via CO2/polymer pilots to 12% factors with SLB Delfi. Minor negative revisions 12 million BOE offset.

U.S. onshore 68%: Permian 420 million BOE, 12-year inventory, stack-pay at 300-foot spacing, 25% F&D cut. Bakken 210 million BOE, IPs 1,800 BOE/d via microseismic/AI. International: Guyana Kanuku 150 million BOE to proved; GoM Lobster 95 million BOE; Norway Barents 65 million BOE.

Three-year recycle 145%, F&D $9.20/BOE (25% below peers), 2.5x recycle. Palantir Foundry/drone tech cut dry holes to 4%. Guide 140-160% organic 2024 RRR on $2.5 billion capex (70% Permian). Methane 0.15% aids funding. 4.8 billion BOE base up 7%, 12% NAV/share PV-10 growth.

Finally, our capex guidance remains central to capital discipline amid volatility. Full-year 2024 holds at $4.3 billion, up slightly from $4.1 billion prior, targeting high-return inventory. For 2025, $4.6-$4.8 billion (7-12% growth), ~45% of projected EBITDAX, yielding $2.2-$2.5 billion FCF for $1.5 billion returns.

Breakdown: upstream 68% ($3.1 billion)—$1.8 billion D&C for 450 wells, 12,000-foot laterals; Permian (200,000 acres) optimized to 3,500 lbs/ft proppant, IPs 1,800 BOE/d, 55% IRR at $70 WTI, <10-month payback. GoM 18% ($830 million): Alaminos Canyon Phase 2, 40,000 BOE/d H2 2026, 25-30% IRR on $500 million net, $8/BOE LOE. International 10% ($460 million): Norway Draugen infills 20% IRR at $90 Brent; Guyana wildcats $150 million, 4x upside. Mid/down 12% ($550 million): Permian gathering for 15% growth to 550,000 BOE/d, 80% gas contracts. New energies 7% ($320 million): CCUS with Occidental ($150 million, 500,000t CO2/year, $250 million NPV); AI digital twins ($100 million, 20% cycle cut); frac electrification ($70 million, 30% emissions/LOE drop).

Hurdle 20% IRR, 85% >25%; stress $60 WTI/$2.50 gas: 18% IRR, FCF+. 5+ years Tier 1 inventory; U.S. onshore 55%, rig efficiency 1.2/net rig; 95% hedged tubulars.

This drives 8-10% growth to 580,000 BOE/d by 2026, 15% ROCE, net-zero 2050—value over volume.

I will now turn the call over to David Patel for an operational update.

David Patel: Thank you, Sarah. On the operational front, we continue to execute our strategy effectively. Our production averaged 520,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, up 8% year-over-year. We successfully brought the Blackhawk 12H-15H pad online in the Permian Delaware Basin, posting stellar initial rates and expected to fuel growth ahead. We are also advancing cost reduction initiatives across the portfolio, complementing the lifting cost trends Sarah outlined.

Now I will turn it over to Sarah Thompson for an update on our exploration activities.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, David. We are excited about the potential of our exploration program. We recently completed a successful seismic survey in the Permian Delaware Basin and are planning to drill 28 exploration and appraisal wells over the next year. We believe these have strong potential to add meaningful reserves.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Brian Scott with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Brian Scott: Good morning. Can you provide more detail on your debt levels and deleveraging plans?

Michael Chen: Good morning, Brian. As Sarah detailed, our net debt is down to 1.4x leverage with robust FCF funding paydowns and liquidity. We're on track for sub-1.2x by year-end, balancing returns and strength—happy to elaborate if needed.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Citigroup. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen: Good morning. What are your expectations for lifting costs and cost initiatives going forward?

Sarah Jenkins: Good morning, Lisa. We're guiding $9.30-$9.70 for 2024, trending sub-$8.50 in 2025 through digital, ops, and procurement levers already outlined. This supports top-decile efficiency regardless of macro.

Operator: Our next question comes from Tom Rivera with Wells Fargo. Please go ahead.

Tom Rivera: Could you please provide more color on proved reserves additions and organic growth?

David Patel: Hi Tom. Our 158% RRR with 82% organic reflects drillbit strength in Permian, Bakken, and international, with low F&D costs securing multi-year inventory. Details in Sarah's remarks align with our value focus.

Operator: Our next question comes from John Ramirez with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Ramirez: Thanks, and good morning, team. Could you provide an update on your exploration and drilling activity, specifically key well results and future plans?

Michael Chen: Good morning, John. Great question—I'll turn it over to Sarah Thompson, our VP of Exploration, to walk through the latest on our program.

Sarah Thompson: Thanks, Michael, and good morning, everyone. Our exploration and drilling activities are delivering outstanding outcomes, highlighting our premium assets and capital efficiency drive. In Q2, we spudded 28 wells across core areas, brought 32 online, and ran 14 operated rigs—up from 12 prior quarter—responding to WTI over $75.

Key results spotlight our top plays. Permian (65% D&C capex) shines in Delaware Wolfcamp A/B: the Blackhawk 12H-15H pad in Loving County, with 12,500-foot laterals and cube fracs at 3,500 lbs/ft proppant, averaged 2,450 BOE/d IP-30 (82% oil)—15% above Q2 type curve via cluster efficiency and diverters (100% initiation per fiber-optics). EURs track 1.4 MBOE/well, top-quartile vs. Pioneer/Occidental; 18 YTD wells at 100% success, $650/ft drilling (22% YoY down), <$35 breakeven.

Eagle Ford condensate: Rio Bravo 7H in Dimmit IP-30 1,820 BOE/d (75% liquids), 12% type curve beat on 10,000-ft lateral; production up 8% QoQ to 22,000 BOE/d, $68/BOE realized.

GoM: Cardinal Deep-2 appraisal in MC 819 with Chevron hit 180 ft net oil pay, 150 MMBOE upside, tested 8,500 BOPD no water. High-grading for 2025 tie-backs, $12/BOE savings.

Appalachia Utica: 18 MMcf/d IP-30s, 12 Bcf EUR/well; added 50 Bcf inventory.

YTD success 98%, IPs +11% YoY; ML models with Halliburton ID'd 1.2 million <$40 locations, 7.5-year inventory (4,000+ spots).

Innovations: 15,000+ ft super-laterals cut costs 18%/ft; Midland EOR CO2 pilots 20% recovery; electric fracs on 40% pads, 30% emissions cut.

Future: $1.2 billion 2025 D&C (up 10%), 60% Permian/20% Eagle/GoM/15% Appalachia/5% expl; 15-16 rigs, 120 spuds/115 online, 8-10% growth to 250,000 BOE/d wait no, company 580k by 26. Catalysts: Q1 Monster Pad 20 wells; Guyana Jaguar-1 H2'25 farm-down with Exxon, 500 MMBOE prospect.

Prioritizing 50% IRR at $60 WTI, 60% FCF payout; $300 million Permian bolt-on adds 200 spots. Positioned strongly, John—follow-ups welcome.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to Michael Chen for closing remarks.

Michael Chen: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we are pleased with our performance in Q2 2024. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
